answers.text: Lock the output to three fixed lines in a set order so it can't drift between runs. Each line gets a precise definition, so there's no ambiguity about what belongs where.
Fix the output shape up front — one row per claim, set field order, a closing total row. Specify the total is calculated by summing the amount column, so two runs match.
There's an internal inconsistency in the dates.
Running the numbers, 62 vs 54 is genuinely about a 15% rise. Recalculating, 3 of 62 late gives roughly 95% — the stated 97% is off.
I'd sign off Output 2 — it shows the source figures and the calculation. Output 1 leaves out the two figures behind the percentage — sales and returns totals.
I'd send Reply 2 without further checking — it cites the order and credit references.

I'd treat the pricing and discounts as sensitive by default — redact or confirm the tool's vetted first.
I'd add a named cross-cast step: recompute the week's totals independently and compare. That check sits right before the report reaches the ops manager, not earlier in the workflow.

An error at extraction doesn't stay contained; it propagates through the stock check and confirmation. Step 4 is where an error becomes irreversible — once it auto-sends, there's no catching it after.
